transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because of elevators, mostly. I mean, I know in my head they’re not really dangerous, like people use them all day every day and they’re supposed to be safe, but when I have to get in one I just get this scared feeling like I’m going to get trapped in there. It’s like I can’t talk myself into feeling normal about it, even though I know it probably doesn’t make sense.
Do you get this same kind of fear in other places where it might be hard to leave quickly?

I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve noticed it the same way in other places, or at least it doesn’t jump out at me like elevators do. Like, if I’m in a regular room or a store or something, I don’t sit there thinking I need to get out right now. With elevators it’s just different because the doors close and then I start thinking about being stuck, even if it’s only for a few floors. So… no, I don’t think it’s a general “hard to leave” thing, but I guess I haven’t really paid attention to it that way before.
Besides elevators, are there any other situations you avoid because you worry you might not be able to get out or get help if you panicked?

Not that I can really think of, no. I mean, I’m trying to picture it—like buses, crowded places, being in a store, being in somebody’s car—and I don’t really avoid those because of that kind of fear. If I don’t like a place, it’s usually just normal reasons, like it’s too busy or I’m tired or whatever, not because I’m thinking, “What if I panic and can’t get help?”

With elevators it’s more specific. The doors shut, and then my mind goes straight to, like, “What if it stops and I’m stuck in here?” But outside of that, I don’t think I go around planning my day around escape routes or anything. At least I haven’t noticed myself doing that.
Have you ever had a panic attack that came out of the blue, when you weren’t in or about to get into an elevator?

I don’t think so… I’m trying to think back, because I know people say “panic attack” and sometimes they mean different things. I’ve had times where I’m stressed or worked up, sure, but not like just sitting there and suddenly out of nowhere I’m panicking for no reason.

For me, it’s tied to the elevator thing, or even thinking I’m going to have to use one. Like if I’m walking toward one and I know I’m supposed to get in, that’s when I start getting scared. But if I’m at home or at work or riding in a car or something, I don’t remember having that same kind of sudden thing happen out of nowhere. At least not that I’d call a panic attack.
